lines.text: Leaving your smartphone sitting on a car dashboard on a sunny day can permanently destroy it in minutes.
On an eighty-degree afternoon, the inside of a closed vehicle can easily spike past one hundred and forty degrees.
Inside your phone, the lithium-ion battery operates with volatile liquid electrolytes.
Extreme heat causes the battery's internal separator film to degrade, triggering thermal runaway.
The battery can swell up like a balloon, cracking the screen glass and risking a chemical fire.
Even if it doesn't catch fire, permanent battery capacity drops by over twenty percent after one afternoon.
Always keep your phone in your pocket or out of direct sunlight.
